text:
Last spring Carolina swept Ottawa in the first round, four games to none. The Senators have spent this season looking like a team that learned something from it: 37 points, 55% of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances), and a 6-2 win in Tampa last night that capped a 3-1-1 week. The question hanging over them is the one the Sens Nation Podcast put in a headline, "The Return Of Backup Goalie Concerns." On the second night of a back-to-back, Samuel Ersson gets the start in place of Linus Ullmark, and Ersson is at an .868 save rate and 5.3 goals below expected this season after finishing 17.8 below expected last year.

That is a hard assignment in Raleigh. The Hurricanes have 41 points and the better chance numbers, 59% of five-on-five expected goals, and they have rested for two days while Ottawa travelled. They have won three straight and took 63% of the chances across their last five. Our numbers do flag that the results have run ahead even of that: a +48 goal difference on +32.8 expected, helped by finishing and by 9.2 goals saved above expected. Pyotr Kochetkov has been a big part of that at +8.6. Sebastian Aho set the Hurricanes' goal record with his 323rd last week, Taylor Hall was honoured for 1,000 games, and Logan Stankoven has 12 points in his last 10. Nikolaj Ehlers is day-to-day and K'Andre Miller is off the injury report.

Ottawa's depth is being tested too. William Eklund is on injured reserve until January, which has pushed Tim Stützle onto a line with Dylan Cozens and Fabian Zetterlund and Ridly Greig up past 18 minutes a night. Greig keeps drawing penalties, and Ottawa draws 5.0 a game while taking 4.6. Graeme Nichols points out one odd number from the team's notes: the Senators have not scored more than one power-play goal in any game this season after doing it 15 times last year.

Michael Amadio has goals in three straight and is one assist from 100 for his career.
headline: Ottawa's backup question meets the Canes' machine
